title: Checks for .to_digit(..).is_some() on chars.
summary: This is a convoluted way of checking if a char is a digit. It’s more straight forward to use the dedicated is_digit method. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for ToString::to_string applied to a type that implements Display in a macro that does formatting.
summary: Since the type implements Display, the use of to_string is unnecessary. Clippy puts this lint in the perf group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for direct implementations of ToString.
summary: This trait is automatically implemented for any type which implements the Display trait. As such, ToString shouldn’t be implemented directly: Display should be implemented instead, and you get the ToString implementation for free. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of todo!.
summary: The todo! macro indicates the presence of unfinished code, so it should not be present in production code. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks if the first paragraph in the documentation of items listed in the module page is too long.
summary: Documentation will show the first paragraph of the docstring in the summary page of a module. Having a nice, short summary in the first paragraph is part of writing good docs. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for functions with too many parameters.
summary: Functions with lots of parameters are considered bad style and reduce readability (“what does the 5th parameter mean?”). Consider grouping some parameters into a new type. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for functions with a large amount of lines.
summary: Functions with a lot of lines are harder to understand due to having to look at a larger amount of code to understand what the function is doing. Consider splitting the body of the function into multiple functions. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for function arguments and let bindings denoted as ref.
summary: The ref declaration makes the function take an owned value, but turns the argument into a reference (which means that the value is destroyed when exiting the function). This adds not much value: either take a reference type, or take an owned value and create references in the body. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.
